$comment: PRE-REGISTERED expected shape for the v3 (state-citation) run. Committed BEFORE the P/B/E namespaces exist and before any v3 recording, for the same reason as pass_bars.json: a prediction written after seeing the numbers is not a prediction. Changing anything here is its own explicit commit that says why.

amendments.what: three namespaces -> four; E- reserved for event-log entries
amendments.why: an id namespace whose meaning changes later makes every recording made under it silently ambiguous

amendments.what: state_coverage gained an explicit denominator; the P/B/E shorthand left over from the three-namespace draft now reads P/B/J in the arms and canary sections. The header keeps its original wording as the historical record of what was committed on 2026-08-14.
amendments.why: the namespaces were built today (tracker task G) and the metric had to be implemented. A denominator chosen while looking at results is not a pre-registration, so it is fixed now, before any v3 recording exists. The shorthand fix is clerical: the 2026-08-15 amendment already moved journey milestones from E- to J- and the arm text was not updated with it.

amendments.what: two properties of the live configuration measured before recording: the model-server LOAD STATE is a hidden variable, and the strip_state_ids lever is not clean in the registered sense
amendments.why: both were found by running the canary and then failing to reproduce its baseline. Recorded here because a reader who meets them in the results would otherwise have to guess whether they were known.
amendments.load_state: A cold model load and a warm one produce DIFFERENT output for identical inputs: same battery, same digest, same (seed, temperature, top_p, num_predict, num_ctx), system_recall 0.5862 / state_coverage 0.5641 cold against 0.6034 / 0.5897 warm. Each state is internally exact — two warm runs matched to 4dp, and a deliberate unload reproduced the cold figures exactly — so it is a variable, not noise. Every run now warms the model first (scripts/record_narration.py), which makes bundles comparable rather than merely annotated. Comparisons WITHIN one process, which is how the canary works, were never affected.
amendments.lever_not_clean: f_recall moves 0.5306 -> 0.6939 when the state ids are removed, against a registered note saying it should be roughly unchanged. f_recall_exclusive — over the 39 must-groups no state id can satisfy — moves with it, 0.4615 -> 0.6154, so this is NOT a mixed alternation being grounded through its profile member instead of its graph one. State ids DISPLACE graph citations for claims with no other citation path. This is the enum-incentive effect f_recall_holds_independently was registered to catch, arriving in the canary rather than in the run. It is a property of the v3 configuration, not a fault in the lever, and the arm's floor is NOT moved to accommodate it.
amendments.implementation_bug_fixed: the clean-lever check was implemented on model_recall, not f_recall as registered. model_recall moves for a second reason — dropping the state ids makes state-only must-groups unreachable, shrinking the denominator without any citation changing — so it was the wrong reading. Corrected to f_recall, which still fires.

the_diagnosis_being_tested.claim: v2's factual_fraction collapse on burden (0.667 -> 0.400) and mitigation (0.933 -> 0.443) is the STATE-CITATION GAP: the model labelled circumstantial segments `feeling` because the schema had no id for a persona's own simulated circumstances. Giving it P/B/J ids should let those segments be `factual` AND cited.
the_diagnosis_being_tested.falsified_if: factual_fraction on burden/mitigation does not recover once the ids exist — the reclassification then had a second cause and the diagnosis was incomplete.

single_declared_variable.changed: prompt v2 -> v3, plus the P/B/J namespaces in the fact-id enum (E- declared and deliberately empty: unsimulated personas carry no event log)
held: seeded fact-order permutation STAYS OFF — reading 5 named it as the lever for position concentration, and turning it on here would entangle two effects and reproduce exactly the unseparable reading v2 produced. It gets its own paired comparison after v3.

model-server load state: WARM. Measured 2026-08-23 as a hidden variable worth ~2 points of system_recall and state_coverage; the recorder now warms the model before scoring so every bundle shares the condition.

arms.$comment: A ceiling as a number would be arbitrary. The discriminator is a control arm: tags whose citable evidence did not change must not move. If everything rises together it is over-correction, however good the burden numbers look.

recovery.expect: factual_fraction recovers toward v1 levels WITH citations attached, not despite them
recovery.ceiling_rationale: at the ceiling every segment is factual, which would mean the persona never merely feels — see feeling_floor. Recovery must come with state ids present, checked by state_coverage below.
recovery.on_miss_low: diagnosis incomplete: the reclassification had a second cause. Do NOT adjust this file to fit; investigate and record what else moved.
recovery.on_miss_high: over-correction: the model is labelling feeling as factual to use the new ids.

control.expect: flat — these are graph-knowledge questions and gained nothing from P/B/J
control.on_miss: if the control tags rise with burden/mitigation, the recovery is over-correction rather than the new ids doing their job.

sym_is_not_a_control.$comment: Symptoms ARE simulated state, so P-citations here are legitimate. sym's factual_fraction rising WITH state ids attached is correct behaviour, not dodging. v2 measured 0.0. No bar; report and read.
sym_is_not_a_control.expect: may rise; must rise only with citations attached

feeling_floor.metric: share of all segments with kind=feeling, across the battery
feeling_floor.rationale: a persona that never merely feels has been schema'd out of personhood. The point of state ids is to let circumstance be grounded, not to abolish the feeling kind.

state_coverage.metric: share of CIRCUMSTANTIAL segments carrying at least one P/B/J id
state_coverage.$comment: The metric that did not exist before this build. It is what the recovery arm has to be caused BY — factual_fraction rising without state ids present is the over-correction signature.

denominator.definition: a segment whose text contains a first-person self-reference AND at least one concrete-world marker from the citation checker's own vocabulary (narration/citations.py FACTUAL_MARKERS)
denominator.kind_independent: DELIBERATE. Scoring only segments the model labelled `factual` would make this metric blind to exactly the v2 pathology it exists to detect: a circumstantial claim relabelled `feeling` to dodge a citation would leave the denominator instead of failing the numerator, and the instrument would report health while the disease continued.
denominator.error_direction: errs toward INCLUDING, which grows the denominator and makes 0.6 harder rather than easier. 'I worry about the side effects' scores as circumstantial though it is really a feeling. Under uncertainty a metric must not flatter itself.
denominator.why_not_a_third_segment_kind: a `circumstance` kind would be a second declared variable in a run whose whole design is one, and the claim being tested is that these segments become `factual` — not that they get a new label.

f_recall_holds_independently.metric: model_recall computed ONLY over questions whose must-set includes F ids
f_recall_holds_independently.rationale: State ids are an easier citation path: a persona's circumstances are always in context, while graph facts must be retrieved and judged relevant. If F-recall dips while state coverage shines, the schema taught the model to ground in ITSELF instead of in knowledge. This is the split-recall lesson applied prospectively instead of after a confounded reading.
f_recall_holds_independently.on_miss: state ids are cannibalising graph citations — a finding about the enum's incentives, not about retrieval.
f_recall_holds_independently.canary_reading_2026_08_23: The canary already shows the effect this arm watches for: removing the state ids raises f_recall 0.5306 -> 0.6939 and f_recall_exclusive 0.4615 -> 0.6154. Baseline f_recall is 0.5306 against this arm's floor of 0.5000 — it clears, with thin margin, and the margin is the finding. The floor stays where it was registered.

inline_marker_takes.$comment: 0/30 in v2; a regression here means prompt v3 reintroduced a formatting convention the schema does not use.

canary_must_fire_first.does: removes the P/B/J ids from the enum and the ABOUT YOU block from the prompt, leaving the v2 configuration: graph F ids only
canary_must_fire_first.rationale: The new axis does not count until the instrument can fail on it. Same rule as the original canary: an eval that cannot fail is decoration. Recording is refused unless this config's state_coverage drops.
canary_must_fire_first.note: F-recall should be roughly UNCHANGED under this config — if it also moves, the lever is not clean and the canary is measuring something other than state ids. Enforced: run_canary refuses `sensitive` unless BOTH truncate_context and strip_state_ids fire, and reports state_lever_clean separately. An unexercised axis (no circumstantial segments at all) is reported as its own verdict rather than as a dead lever — that is a finding about the battery, not the instrument.
canary_must_fire_first.implementation: build_prompt(include_state_facts=False), threaded through evaluation.score as the `strip_state_ids` degradation so the degraded run traverses the same code path as a real one

authoring_protocol.$comment: The battery's state-citation expectations are AUTHORED, not generated. Recorded here because how they were authored determines what the eval measures.
rules: Author blind from state dumps — profile, derived barriers, event log — never from recorded takes. Authoring from model output measures stability, not relevance; it is the trap this eval already fell into once and it is most seductive when the takes are fresh and good.

Author must/may sets, never exact sets. Recall grades against the must-set; the may-set exempts reasonable citations from counting against precision. An exact set converts the eval from 'is this grounded' into 'does the model agree with the author'.
A question with no correct state id is a FINDING about the event log's coverage, not an eval inconvenience. Log it; never stretch an id to fit.
Must-sets minimal — usually one to three ids: the thing the answer is ABOUT, not everything true of the persona.
A derivation chain gives an ALTERNATION, not a conjunction. B-x or its origin P-y satisfies grounding; the must-set names one and the may-set holds the other.
Uncertain whether an id is must or may -> may. A must-set the author is unsure of grades the model against the author's hesitation.

Inherited F-expectations are REVIEWED, not inherited. Some were authored when F was the only namespace and may have been stretched to cover circumstance that P/B/J now express properly; those move to may or drop. A question's F must-set may legitimately be empty — which is why f_recall_holds_independently grades only over questions whose must-sets include F ids.

namespaces.$comment: AMENDED 2026-08-15, before any v3 recording and before the enum was built — legitimate precisely because nothing is recorded yet. Originally three namespaces with E- covering journey milestones. Split into four.
namespaces.J: journey milestones — e.g. J-diagnosis, J-adverse_event. What the battery grounds in TODAY.

E.meaning: simulation event-log entries — visits attended/missed, burden accrual, dropout
E.why_not_folded_into_J: An id namespace whose meaning changes later is an artifact that acquires semantics from whoever reads it — the same failure as a baseline defaulting its runtime stamp from the reader. Cassettes recorded against a journey-E would go silently ambiguous the day simulated personas enter the battery carrying real event logs, and click-through would have to disambiguate two provenance types under one prefix. That is the blur the room's badge work just removed. Four namespaces cost nothing under constrained decoding: the enum is the enum.
E.consequence: A question that wants 'you missed visit 3' has NO id for an unsimulated persona. That is a coverage finding to log, not an id to stretch.
